The paper "Next-Generation Cobalt-Free Cathodes – A Prospective Solution to the Battery Industry's Cobalt Problem" estimates how much cobalt would be needed to build a million electric vehicles with different cathodes.

For NMC 111, it estimates that nearly 10 kilotons of cobalt are needed to produce 1 million EVs.

For NMC 811/NCA, it estimates that producing >150 million EVs by 2050 would require more than 2.5 million metric tons of usable cobalt, which represents more than one third of the known global Co reserves (≈7 million metric tons).

prompt.system: You answer questions using only the documents below: pages selected from them, with tables written row by row. Answer briefly. If you compute a number, show the calculation. If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: adma-2020 (LiNixFeyAlzO2, NFA): ≈2500 tons for NMC 111, ≈700 tons for NMC 811 and NCA, none for NFA (BatPaC; 260 miles) (p2.L84-104)
